PullRequest.Title: Add editor part `supportsSplitting` capability and hide "Open to the Side" where it is unsupported
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #315740

## Problem

The Agents window has a single editor group and doesn't support splitting. Quick access still offers "Open to the Side" in Go to Symbol in Editor (`@`), Quick Open (`Ctrl+P`) and Go to Symbol in Workspace (`#`). Clicking it, or using Alt / Ctrl+Enter, does nothing visible.

## Root cause

dbgjs on the Agents window renderer showed what happens when you click the button:
- `GotoSymbolQuickAccessProvider.gotoLocation` takes the side branch and calls `openEditor(…, SIDE_GROUP)`.
- That goes to `findGroup` and then `DesktopMainEditorPart.addGroup`.
- The Agents-window part overrides `addGroup` to return the same group, so the number of groups stays at 1 and the editor reopens in place.
- The pickers had no way to know the part can't split. They always showed the button.

## Change

Splitting support is now a capability of the editor part, which consumers read. It replaces per-feature window checks.

**The capability**
- `IEditorGroupsContainer.supportsSplitting` (new, readonly).
- `EditorPart` returns `true`.
- `EditorParts` delegates to the active part.
- The Agents window's `DesktopMainEditorPart` overrides it to `false`.
- Its editor drop target now passes `supportsSplitting: this.supportsSplitting` (the existing `IEditorDropTargetDelegate.supportsSplitting` option) instead of a hard-coded `false`.

**Consumers that now read it**
- Go to Symbol in Editor: `openSideBySideDirection` returns `undefined` when splitting is unsupported, so the base provider doesn't add the button. The side branch in `gotoLocation` is gated too.
- Quick Open (`AnythingQuickAccessProvider`): the "Open to the Side" button on file, editor-history and link picks is gated, and so is the side-group target (`openToSide` / `SIDE_GROUP`). The "Remove from History" button index adjusts.
- Go to Symbol in Workspace (`SymbolsQuickAccessProvider`): the button and the side-group target are gated.

When the part can't split, Alt / Ctrl+Enter / the button fall back to opening in the active group.

**Not in this PR**
These places still check the window type directly and could move to this capability in follow-ups:
- multi-diff editor actions;
- survey;
- native issue form;
- `emptyFileEditorSearch`;
- generic `SIDE_GROUP` callers such as explorer "Open to the Side".

## How tested

- `scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/codeEditor/test/browser/gotoSymbolQuickAccess.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/test/browser/anythingQuickAccess.test.ts`: 51 passing. New tests cover:
  - no side button and no side-group open when `supportsSplitting` is false, for Go to Symbol;
  - no "Open to the Side" button on Quick Open picks.
- `pnpm run oxlint <the 10 changed files>`: clean.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- UI scenario in the Agents window (Linux): open `src/app.ts` in a session, run Go to Symbol (`@`) and Quick Open (`package`), hover the row and click "Open to the Side" if it is shown.
  - **Before** (Insiders 1.146.0-insider): both pickers show the button; clicking it leaves 1 editor group and reopens in place.
  - **After** (dev build of this branch): neither picker shows the button; Enter opens in place.

The dev-build recording needed a local tweak to the built `out/` protocol handler to work around a flaky `vscode-file://` load failure on the test machine. That tweak is not part of this change.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added line is directly inside the result loop, and the getter chain proves the repeated allocations, focus queries, and part scan. Provider result count varies, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, document.hasFocus calls, editor-part scans, and temporary document arrays
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(S * (W + P)) per query for S deduplicated symbols surviving filtering, W registered windows, and P editor parts; previously this added cost was absent.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased picker-update latency and CPU/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The symbol loop created the side button unconditionally and did not perform an editor-part or active-window lookup per result.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every retained workspace-symbol result now evaluates editorGroupService.supportsSplitting while its pick is constructed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 207 adds `this.editorGroupService.supportsSplitting` to each pick created by the workspace-symbol loop.
Findings.Title: Snapshot splitting support before converting workspace symbols
Findings.Impact: With an auxiliary editor window open, workspace-symbol searches repeat focus detection and allocation for every result on each query, adding synchronous CPU and GC work to picker updates and degrading typing responsiveness in symbol-heavy workspaces.
Findings.Evidence: The condition is inside the loop over the deduplicated output of getWorkspaceSymbols. EditorParts.supportsSplitting delegates through activePart; MultiWindowParts.activePart calls getActiveDocument and getPartByDocument. With multiple registered windows, getActiveDocument allocates document arrays and calls document.hasFocus, after which getPartByDocument scans registered parts. The whole lookup therefore repeats before the picker receives each result batch.
Findings.Recommendation: Read supportsSplitting once after the awaited symbol query and before the loop, then reuse that snapshot for the whole result batch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Go to Symbol in Workspace (`#`) and workspace-symbol results merged into Quick Open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the typing delayer, all workspace-symbol providers return; the UI then synchronously filters and converts the deduplicated symbol collection before picks can be displayed. The new supportsSplitting read is on this conversion critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke registered workspace-symbol providers, which may be extension-host providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent call per registered provider per query; provider outputs are deduplicated before conversion
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider fan-out existed before; the diff adds repeated active-window discovery only during conversion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider calls must settle before synchronous pick conversion starts

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search workspace files for Quick Open
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one search per query, with a second full-query search when a multi-part query hits the result limit; cached queries reuse the existing search cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File search count and placement are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with workspace-symbol retrieval before merged picks are produced

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is the deduplicated provider output that survives fuzzy/container filtering. It can contain hundreds or more symbols; conversion is repeated for each query.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace symbol providers run concurrently through Promise.all, but result conversion is one synchronous loop. Quick Open runs file and symbol retrieval in parallel, then merges and caps displayed results at 512; the new per-symbol work occurs before that cap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache for the new capability read. The workspace-symbol provider results and fuzzy processing follow existing behavior; each fresh query repeats conversion. Snapshotting the capability once per completed query preserves the active-part value for that batch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed condition is inside the symbol loop and delegates through activePart to getActiveDocument and a part scan.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact symbol counts and the cost of document.hasFocus vary by installed providers and number of open windows, but the repeated allocation/focus-query mechanism is explicit and unbounded by the Quick Open display cap.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: every retained symbol repeats multi-window focus discovery and allocations; snapshot the capability once per result batch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Quick Open file, editor-history, and link picks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: History and file results are converted to picks before rendering; accepting a pick then opens the resource. Link-handler discovery must finish before contributed link picks appear. The new capability checks affect pick construction and target-group selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two searches for a multi-part query that hits the 512-result limit; otherwise one, with existing cache reuse
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical file-search calls occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before additional file picks are rendered

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery call for a valid pasted link query
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same handler discovery occurred before; only the side-opening flag/button is now gated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before link picks are returned

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open an accepted HTTP(S) link through the opener or selected handler
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per explicit user accept
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same open operation occurred before; the diff only changes whether it requests a side group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after selection and does not delay pick construction

Scenarios.ScalingInput: File search is capped at 512 results and history scales with retained editor history; links scale with the small set of registered handlers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File and optional workspace-symbol searches run in parallel. File-result conversion is synchronous; accepts are user-triggered one at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing file-query and fuzzy-score caches remain intact. Cold file searches cross the search-service boundary; warm cached searches reuse the prior cache. The capability itself is not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added reads and unchanged boundaries; lower magnitude for bounded file/history result conversion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new createAnythingPick capability read repeats for bounded file/history collections in multi-window sessions, but the cap and inexpensive single-window path do not independently establish a user-visible regression beyond the reported unbounded symbol path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: boundary counts and caching are unchanged, and the per-file/history capability read is bounded. The workspace-symbol sub-scenario is covered by the reported finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Go to Symbol in Editor (`@`) and accepting a local symbol
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing document-symbol/outline retrieval produces picks; evaluating the side-button direction and accepting a pick then synchronously reads supportsSplitting before either opening to the side or revealing in the active editor.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The capability getter is evaluated at option/render access and once on accept, not once per local symbol in the changed workbench code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing symbol retrieval and cancellation behavior are unchanged; acceptance is a single user action with no new queue or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced or defeated. The capability is read live so it follows the currently active editor part.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code adds constant-time capability gating around existing UI and open paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying language providers may have their own costs, but this diff neither adds nor multiplies those calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the added reads are constant cardinality and can avoid an unnecessary side-group open attempt in unsupported parts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor drag/drop target creation in the single-group Agents desktop editor part
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drop-target construction forwards the new capability value to the existing superclass; the getter returns the constant false directly.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One read per drop-target creation, independent of editor or symbol collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous construction with no changed concurrency or scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; the value is a constant override.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; this is a direct constant getter substitution for the previous hard-coded false.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: behavior and cost are equivalent to the previous hard-coded option.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. One medium repeated-work issue was submitted for per-symbol active-window discovery; no cache, boundary fan-out, eager-work, lifecycle, concurrency, or retained-memory regression was otherwise established.
